chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Being called in at the Savoy against Chick Webb, but not hired
summary: At the Savoy in New York the band called her in to break up Chick Webb's cutting contest, yet she was not made a regular member, partly because of the pianist Jack and because a woman was unusual.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: How did you happen to become a regular member of the band?

Well, we scuffled. Let's see, we went to the Savoy in New York. By this time we were playing "Froggy Bottom" and things like that. They called me in to sing because Chick Webb was really blasting town with all bands and they were getting rid of all bands that came in there. I guess you heard about that era; it was sensational. When he came in you just prayed that you'd go over.
So they called for me and I'd be out in the car, I'd be downstairs playing miniature golf, and I'd go up and break it up, 'cause I was so tiny.
Mary, if you all these years have been breaking it up on this basis of being called in specially, why did they never put you on a regular basis?

Well, because they had this pianist. They respected him. Jack was a nice guy. Number one, Jack - I don't know his name - Jack Somebody. He was a good man and everything. It may have been that they didn't want a woman in the band because women during that era was not playing with men. That was another thing that made people scream and carry on, because they saw a woman and one that weighed 90 pounds. My feet was just barely touching the floor. That was a good point about it, but to hear me play so heavy like a man, that was something else. I don't know why John wasn't pushing it but he was through. He was putting me like, you know, in position. He had me on the scene. But I tell you what happened. We worked with Blanche Calloway in Philadelphia. This was before I joined the band. Whenever they went on tours I was with them. We went to Philadelphia; we worked for the Steeple there. You've heard about that. They were Ethel Waters, Bill Bailey -
